```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "B is pure software. The brief says SplitKin, TendTo and CircleCare were built by one- or two-person teams, so a solo build with AI agents inside 90 days is plausible. A depends on sourcing, warehousing, customs, breakage and failed addresses, and A's own case against concedes that AI agents don't solve these.",
    "B has more and better-sourced demand evidence. Three sourced Reddit quotes describe ongoing pain, such as tracking medications in Google Sheets and calendars and group threads that weren't built for caregiving. A has one LinkedIn comment plus a seed HN quote that the brief never reproduces.",
    "B's price point is set by at least five competitors charging $3.99 to $24.99 a month for the same feature set. A's evidence suggests the category sells on enterprise terms, around $15k to $20k+ a year for Sendoso. That is a poor fit for a solo founder chasing a first self-serve payer.",
    "B has near-zero-cost ways to reach a first customer: r/CaregiverSupport and r/AgingParents, where people already ask for app recommendations. A's sourced channels are Stripe Marketplace, which requires passing app review, and paid social at $150 to $250 per MQL/SQL, which is costly against a cheap narrow product.",
    "B's weaknesses mainly limit how big the business can get: dense competition, users who want it free, short customer lifetime and siblings who must also adopt it. They still allow a first paying customer. A's weaknesses (incumbents already offer event-triggered swag, physical fulfillment risk, $30 to $75 per kit on top of the subscription) threaten the first sale itself."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea A's demand evidence rests on one LinkedIn comment from someone who received Stripe's gift and was asking which vendor sent it. That shows curiosity, not a buyer with a need or budget. The 'seed HN quote' is mentioned but never shown, so it counts as missing. The case-for assumption that an 'existing swag-fulfillment API' can be wired to a Stripe webhook is also unsourced.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. B's crowded market, users' explicit preference for free tools and short customer lifetime are real risks to a viable business. Neither brief shows conversion data proving people actually pay; competitor price lists show asking prices, not sales. B wins because the 90-day bar is a single paying customer, and B's software-only build and near-zero-cost community channels clear that bar more plausibly than A's logistics-heavy, enterprise-priced category."
}
```
